TITLE:
Economies of Scale:
Why Bigger Batches
Cost Less Per Unit
LEAD: Building a factory, buying the equipment, running the R&D — those costs are fixed whether you make 100 units or 100,000. Spread that same fixed cost across more units and the per-unit share of it keeps shrinking, which is why the 10,000th unit is so much cheaper to make than the 100th. It doesn't fall forever, though: past some volume, coordination overhead, logistics complexity, and management layers start adding their own cost per unit back in — diseconomies of scale, the point where bigger stops meaning cheaper.
